<b>Наружный нос.</b> Верхнюю треть спинк: External nose. The paired nasal bones support the upper third of the bridge; below is a framework of cartilages: the lateral ones (extensions of the septal cartilage) and the major alar ones, which shape the tip and the nostril rims. The wings are dense fatty tissue without cartilage. Inside the nostril, the vestibule has stiff hairs that trap coarse dust.
<b>Носовая перегородка</b> делит полость: The nasal septum divides the cavity into two halves. In front it is cartilage, behind it is bone: the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid above and the vomer below. Almost every adult has at least a slightly deviated septum. Low in front lies Kiesselbach’s area, where branches of four arteries meet; most nosebleeds start here.
<b>Носовые раковины</b> — три костных за: The nasal conchae (turbinates) are three bony scrolls on the lateral wall, covered with mucosa. The superior and middle ones are parts of the ethmoid bone; the inferior one is a separate bone. They multiply the mucosal surface several times and swirl the airflow. The mucosa of the inferior concha holds venous plexuses: when they swell, the nasal passage narrows.
<b>Носовые ходы</b> — щели под раковинам: The nasal meatuses are the gaps under the conchae. The frontal and maxillary sinuses and the anterior ethmoidal cells open into the middle meatus through the semilunar hiatus; the posterior cells open into the superior meatus, and the sphenoidal sinus above the superior concha. The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus — that is why your nose runs when you cry.
<b>Обонятельная область</b> — около 2,5: The olfactory region is about 2.5 cm² of mucosa on each side under the roof of the nose. It holds several million olfactory neurons; their processes — the olfactory nerves (cranial nerve I) — pass through the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb. The neurons are replaced every 1–2 months.
<b>Носоглотка.</b> Через хоаны — два зад: Nasopharynx. Through the choanae — two rear openings — the nasal cavity leads into the throat. On its side wall is the opening of the auditory (eustachian) tube, which leads to the middle ear; that is why a cold can block your ears. On its roof is the pharyngeal tonsil; in children it often enlarges (adenoids) and makes nose breathing hard.
<b>Лобные пазухи</b> — в лобной кости на: The frontal sinuses lie in the frontal bone above the bridge of the nose, behind the brow ridges. They are usually asymmetric and separated by a septum; a few percent of people lack one or both. They drain through the frontonasal duct into the front end of the middle meatus. Behind, their wall borders the anterior cranial fossa; below, the orbit.
<b>Решётчатые ячейки</b> — «соты» из 3–1: The ethmoidal cells are a “honeycomb” of 3–18 air spaces in the ethmoid bone between the orbits. The anterior and middle cells open into the middle meatus, the posterior ones into the superior meatus. Only a paper-thin plate (lamina papyracea) separates them from the orbit: in children, ethmoid inflammation can spread to the orbital tissues.
<b>Верхнечелюстная (гайморова) пазуха</b: The maxillary sinus is the largest, about 15 ml: a pyramid in the body of the maxilla below the orbit. Its opening sits high on the inner wall, so mucus is carried up to it by cilia, not drained by gravity. Its floor is close to the roots of the upper premolars and molars, so a tooth infection can spread into the sinus.
<b>Клиновидная пазуха</b> — в теле клино: The sphenoidal sinus lies in the body of the sphenoid bone, deepest of all, behind the nasal cavity; a septum splits it into two unequal parts. It opens above the superior concha. Above it is the sella turcica with the pituitary gland; at its sides run the optic nerves and internal carotid arteries. Surgeons reach pituitary tumors through the nose by way of this sinus.
<b>Новорождённый.</b> Пазухи только закл: Newborn. The sinuses are only just forming: there are a few small ethmoidal cells and tiny maxillary sinuses — narrow slits in the lateral wall of the nose. There are no frontal or sphenoidal sinuses yet. A baby’s face is short: the tooth buds lie almost right under the orbits.
<b>Первые годы.</b> Верхнечелюстные пазу: First years. The maxillary sinuses grow with the maxilla and spread sideways beneath the orbits. At around 2–3 years air begins to enter the body of the sphenoid bone, and the sphenoidal sinus starts to form. The number of ethmoidal cells increases.
<b>Дошкольный возраст.</b> Из одной из п: Preschool years. The frontal sinus grows upward into the frontal bone from one of the anterior ethmoidal cells; it usually shows on an X-ray by age 7–8. The sphenoidal sinus enlarges and extends back under the sella turcica.
<b>Школьные годы.</b> Зубы сменяются, и: School years. The teeth are replaced, and the sinus takes over the space freed in the maxilla: by 8–12 years its floor drops to the level of the nasal floor. The ethmoidal labyrinth almost reaches adult size.
<b>Подростки.</b> В период полового созр: Teenagers. During puberty the frontal sinuses grow especially fast — together with the brow ridges, more in boys. The floor of the maxillary sinus sinks below the nasal floor, toward the tooth roots.
<b>Взрослый.</b> Рост пазух заканчиваетс: Adult. The sinuses stop growing by 18–20 years; their size and shape vary greatly from person to person. In old age, after teeth are lost, the maxillary sinus may expand further into the alveolar process.
<b>Полость носа</b> — начало дыхательных: The nasal cavity is the start of the airway. More than 10,000 liters of air pass through the nose every day: here it is cleaned, warmed and humidified, and up under the roof it is “tasted” for smell. Shown is the right half, viewed from the side of the removed septum; the dots are the inhaled airflow. Click a part or choose it below.
<b>Околоносовые пазухи</b> — полости с в: The paranasal sinuses are air spaces in the bones around the nose: frontal, ethmoidal, maxillary and sphenoidal. They are lined with the same mucosa as the nose, and cilia sweep mucus toward narrow openings in the nasal meatuses. The sinuses lighten the skull and probably affect the timbre of the voice. Choose a sinus to see how it drains.
Нос — не просто вход для воздуха: ракови: The nose is more than an air intake: the conchae swirl the flow, the mucosa warms and humidifies it, cilia carry dust away, and right under the roof live the olfactory neurons. Around it are four pairs of sinuses — hollow “rooms” in the bones of the face.
\n <div><h2>Устройство</h2>\n:
Structure

The nasal cavity opens to the outside through the nostrils and backward through the choanae into the nasopharynx. Its floor is the hard palate, its roof the narrow cribriform plate, its inner wall the septum, and its lateral wall carries the conchae and meatuses. The vestibule is lined with hairy skin, the rest of the cavity with ciliated respiratory mucosa, and the roof with olfactory mucosa.

Smell is carried by the olfactory nerve (I). Pain, touch and temperature travel in branches of the trigeminal nerve: the anterior ethmoidal (V₁) and the nasopalatine and posterior nasal nerves (V₂). Blood comes from the sphenopalatine artery (a branch of the maxillary), the anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteries (from the ophthalmic), the greater palatine artery and branches of the facial artery.

How the nose works

Mucus traps dust and microbes, and the cilia, beating 10–15 times a second, sweep it back into the throat at about 5–10 mm a minute — we swallow it without noticing. As air passes through the meatuses, it is warmed almost to body temperature and saturated with moisture. Only a small part of each breath reaches the olfactory cleft — that is why we sniff to pick up a smell.

The mucosa of the conchae swells and shrinks in turn: every few hours one half of the nose breathes more freely than the other (the “nasal cycle”). We usually don’t notice it.

Medicine

  • Runny nose (rhinitis) — swollen mucosa and excess mucus; usually viral, sometimes allergic.
  • Sinusitis — inflammation of the sinuses, usually when swelling closes the narrow openings in the middle meatus. The maxillary sinus is affected most often.
  • Nosebleed — most often from Kiesselbach’s area. First aid: sit down, lean your head forward and pinch the soft part of the nose for 10–15 minutes; do not tilt the head back.
  • A deviated septum and polyps obstruct breathing and sinus drainage; they are corrected surgically.
  • Loss of smell (anosmia) can follow viral infections or injury to the cribriform plate, and can be an early sign of some brain diseases.
